title: India, UAE ink major pacts on energy, defence, AI; Abu Dhabi commits $5 billion investment
source_used: DD News (citing India's Ministry of External Affairs)
key_facts: India and the UAE signed agreements on energy, defence, maritime infrastructure and emerging technologies during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Abu Dhabi.

The UAE announced $5 billion of investment in India: $3 billion by Emirates New Development Bank in RBL Bank, $1 billion by ADIA with NIIF in infrastructure, $1 billion by International Holding Company in Sammaan Capital.
C-DAC (India's Centre for Development of Advanced Computing) and UAE-based G42 will set up an 8-exaflop supercomputing cluster to support India's AI Mission.
A Framework for Strategic Defence Partnership covers industrial collaboration, advanced technologies, maritime security, cyber defence, training, secure communications and information exchange.

ADNOC and Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited agreed to widen UAE participation in India's strategic oil reserves and explore strategic gas reserves; IOCL and ADNOC finalised a long-term LPG supply arrangement.
Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World agreed a ship repair cluster at Vadinar.
quote_evidence: India and the United Arab Emirates on Friday signed a series of agreements across energy, defence, maritime infrastructure and emerging technologies during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Abu Dhabi, with the Gulf nation announcing investments worth $5 billion in India.
the two sides announced a partnership between C-DAC and UAE-based G42 to establish an 8 Exaflop Super Compute Cluster to support India's AI Mission and advanced computing capabilities.
the two countries signed a Framework for Strategic Defence Partnership aimed at deepening industrial collaboration and expanding cooperation in advanced technologies, maritime security, cyber defence
why_it_matters_hint: Ties a Gulf investor and AI firm to India's AI computing plans and defence industry.
event_date: Article says 'Friday' (9 Oct 2026) but was published 8 Oct 2026 19:41 UTC; date unclear
notes: DD News is India's state broadcaster; facts come from the Ministry of External Affairs. Day of signing unclear (article says Friday, publication stamp is Thursday 8 Oct). Weekday left out of the entry. Dollar figures and the 8-exaflop number are as announced; no delivery date given.
